column2: E + 1-3 digits; Class A 1-129, Class B 130+ (links)
column3: Reference roads: E-W end in 0, N-S end in 5. Intermediate roads take numbers between the reference roads they sit between.
column4: E-W = even, N-S = odd. E-W numbers rise from north to south (E10 far north, E90 far south). N-S numbers rise from west to east (E05 far west). Main exceptions: E4 and E6 run N-S.
column6: Many countries sign the E number next to the national one; Belgium, Norway, Sweden, Denmark lean on E numbers; the UK and Albania do not sign them.

column2: Own island system (no E, A prefixes)
column3: Separate local system using numbers 1-4 plus a few 2- and 3-digit numbers
column6: Treat as Finland-style signs but with its own low numbers.

column2: A = motorway (green signs), SH = state road (blue signs)
column3: SH roads form the main network; A1 also carries SH10; SH1 runs Tirana to Han i Hotit in the north
column6: Blue SH shields = ordinary state roads; green A = motorway.

column2: CG = Carretera General
column3: CG-1 runs Andorra la Vella to Spain; CG-2 runs to France; CG-3 and CG-4 climb to Arcalis and Pal
column5: Numbers 1-4 fan out from the capital
column6: CG-1 = south to Spain, CG-2 = north/east to France.

column2: A motorway, S expressway, B/L provincial (former federal B roads)
column3: A1-A4 start in Vienna; A7-A14 lie west of Vienna and their numbers grow with distance; S1-S99 short expressways
column5: A1-A4 radiate from Vienna; main B roads 1-10 leave Vienna clockwise
column6: Low A numbers (1-4) mean Vienna corridors.

column2: E, M (main), R (regional), N/H local
column3: M1 is the main east-west route; M2-M7 radiate from Minsk; M9 is the Minsk ring
column6: Cyrillic P and H are R and N.
column7: Partial; source from 2007, some numbers changed after

column2: E, A motorway, R ring, N national, B links, P provincial
column3: A1-A10 run clockwise from Brussels (A1 north). N1-N9 form a clockwise spider web (N1 Brussels-Antwerp). Two-digit N ending in 0 are lateral links; 3-digit numbers start with a province digit (1 Antwerp, 2 Brabant, 3 W. Flanders, 4 E. Flanders, 5 Hainaut, 6 Liege, 7 Limburg, 8 Luxembourg, 9 Namur)
column5: Clockwise from Brussels; R0 = Brussels ring
column6: E numbers appear alone on motorways, A numbers are less visible.

column2: E, A motorway (A1/A2), M main, R local (4xx)
column3: One-digit M roads run east-west (NW-SE); two-digit M roads run north-south; 2-digit numbers rise eastward; 4xx is the Bosnian zone
column4: One digit = E-W, two digits = N-S (loose)
column6: A 3-digit R number starting with 4 is a Bosnian local road.

column2: E, A motorway (A1, A2, A4, A5), national roads (plain numbers)
column3: Derived routes add digits to the parent number (2 -> 27, 73 -> 7301)
column4: 2, 4, 6, 8 run E-W, rising southward; 1, 5, 7, 9 run N-S, rising eastward
column6: Single-digit plain numbers = main grid roads.

column2: A motorway (1-11), B fast road, D state road, Z county, L local, E
column3: One-digit D roads are main cross-country routes; 3-digit D: first digit sets a zone (1 islands, 2 border crossings, 3 mostly Istria, 4 west of D8, 5 rest); D8 is the coast road. Z roads zones: 1 Zagreb, 2 Varazdin, 3 Sisak, 4 east, 5 west, 6 south
column4: One-digit D: odd numbers rise eastward, even rise southward
column6: D8 = Adriatic coast road.

column2: A motorway (A1-A9), B main road, E regional, F local
column3: E and F numbers start with the number of a nearby B road. Motorway exit numbers are unique nationwide, each motorway has its own range (A1 1-29, A2 30-39, A5 40-49, A3 50-59, A6 70-79)
column6: Check exit number to know which motorway you are on.

column2: E, D motorway, R expressway, 1-3 digit national roads, ring roads in some cities
column3: Numbers rise clockwise; 3-digit national roads take the zone from the first digit. When a bypass replaces an old road the old number is often raised by 600
column5: Routes 1-12 radiate from Prague like a spider web; 13-99 other main roads
column6: D1 = Prague-Brno-Ostrava corridor.

column2: E (no national numbers), 1-2 digit primary roads (motorways), 3-digit secondary roads, O ring roads
column3: Secondary 3-digit numbers: 1xx main secondary; 2xx Sjaelland/Lolland; 3xx Fyn/Langeland; 4xx South Jutland; 5xx North Jutland. Ring roads rise from the centre
column6: Most Danish motorways show E numbers only.

column2: E (only E20, E67, E77), national roads 1-88, community roads T-xxxxx
column3: Main roads 1-10 form a spider web (1, 2 and 4 start in Tallinn); basic roads 11-88 are in clusters sharing a first digit; community road first two digits = county
column6: Single-digit road = main road.

column2: Route numbers only (10, 11, 40, 50, 52, 60 ...)
column3: Route 10 is the main route out of Torshavn towards Klaksvik; route 11 goes to the Vagar airport; route 50 is Oyggjarvegur; route 60 links Streymoy and Sandoy
column6: Route 10 is the backbone; look for route numbers in a box on signs.

column2: E, Vt (1-2 digit main), Kt (2-digit), Mt (3-4 digit), Pt local, Kehä ring roads
column3: Routes 1-7 fan out from Helsinki, 8-10 from Turku, 11-12 from Tampere, 13-15 once radiated from Vyborg. 3-5 digit numbers generally rise northward. Four-digit numbers often extend a 3-digit number
column6: Low 1-digit number = main road out of Helsinki.

column2: A motorway, N national (red shield), D departmental (yellow), E, T (Corsica)
column3: N1-N17 run clockwise around Paris starting with N1 north (Point zero at Notre-Dame); higher N numbers keep circling Paris. Motorways: first digit is a zone (1 Paris, 2 north, 3 north-east, 4 east, 5 south-east, 6 south-west, 7 south-central, 8 west). Each department numbers its own D roads
column6: A6/A7 are the 'Sun motorways' (Paris to Lyon to Marseille).

column2: A motorway (blue), B federal road (yellow), L/K state and district, E
column3: Autobahn: 1-digit = national, 2-digit = regional, 3-digit = local; first digit of 2-3 digits is a zone that generally increases southward. B roads: 1-10 cross the country, then regional blocks numbered in a clockwise sweep (B11-B26 Bavaria etc.)
column4: Autobahn: even = E-W (numbers rise north to south), odd = N-S (numbers rise west to east); some exceptions
column6: A7 is the longest N-S Autobahn; A8 is the main E-W road in the south.

column2: Very few roads
column3: Not covered
column6: Treat like a UK-style small territory.

column2: E, A motorway, national roads (plain numbers 1-2 digits)
column3: Motorway numbers assigned in ranges; exit numbers are unique nationwide and numbered as exits are added
column4: Odd = N-S, even = E-W (exceptions like Route 1 Athens-Macedonia). Two-digit national: odd rise eastward, even rise southward
column6: Route 1 is Athens-Thessaloniki; A1 follows it.

column2: E, M motorway/expressway, plain-number national roads 1-5 digits
column3: Routes 1-8 are the main arterials from Budapest (route 1 runs west). A number starting with x lies between route x and x+1; numbers starting with 8 lie between 1 and 8. Motorway numbers match national numbers except M0 (Budapest ring)
column5: Radial from Budapest, zones between arterials
column6: M1 west, M3 east, M5 south-east, M7 south-west from Budapest.

column2: National roads 1-3 digits, F mountain roads (gravel)
column3: Route 1 is the ring road. First digit is a zone 2-9 running clockwise from zone 2 in the south; Reykjavik is zone 4, Akureyri zone 8
column6: F roads are always unsurfaced and highland-only.

column2: M motorway, N national (1-32 primary, 50-87 secondary), R regional, L local, E
column3: Spider web radiating from Dublin; N numbers sweep around Dublin; regional first digit: R1 Dublin, R2 north, R3 west, R4 centre, R5 south-west, R6 south, R7 south-east. Motorway kilometre posts count towards Dublin
column4: N12-N25 run from north to south as seen from Dublin
column6: N-number order tells you the compass slice from Dublin; N7 south-west, N11 south-east.

column2: A roads (A1, A2 ...)
column3: Not covered
column6: Look for UK-style A/B signs.

column2: E, A motorway, SS state road, SR regional, SP provincial
column3: A1-A32 numbered sequentially. SS1-SS8 form a spider web around Rome (SS1 clockwise to SS8). SS10-SS112 run north to south, Sicily 113-124, Sardinia 125-134, then the count restarts in the north from 141. Each province numbers its own SP roads
column6: A1 = Autostrada del Sole Milan-Rome-Naples.

column2: A roads (A1 ...)
column3: A1 connects St Helier and St Aubin; wider rules not covered
column6: Parish roads are mostly unnumbered.

column2: R motorway (R6, R7), N national (N2 Pristina-Mitrovica), E
column3: Older M numbers (M-2, M-9, M-25) appear on older sources; N numbers replaced them
column6: Motorways R7 to Albania and R6 to North Macedonia leave Pristina.
column7: Partial; two sources, rules not found

column2: E67, A main roads (A1-A15), P first-class, V second-class
column3: A1, A2, A3 and A6-A10 radiate clockwise from Riga; A4/A5 are Riga bypasses; A11-A15 further out. P numbers start at P1 near Riga and rise eastward, then southward, then westward
column6: A1 is Via Baltica to Estonia (north).

column2: A (Swiss-style), main roads numbered by Switzerland
column3: Falls under the Swiss system
column6: Swiss-style signs.

column2: E, A main roads (A1-A16), regional (1xx/2xx), municipal
column3: A1-A4 run clockwise from Vilnius; higher number = further from Vilnius; regional 2xx = ring roads and bypasses
column6: A1 Vilnius-Kaunas-Klaipeda.

column2: E, A motorway, B single-digit links (B3, B7), N national, CR local
column3: N1-N7 and N11 run clockwise around the capital; A1, A3, A4, A6, A7 leave Luxembourg City; A13 runs west-east. CR 1xx south, 3xx north
column6: N-number and A-number often share the same corridor.

column2: No national numbered system found
column3: Roads known by name and place
column6: Use place names, not numbers.

column2: Not covered
column3: Not covered
column6: Not covered.

column2: M main roads, R regional roads, A motorway
column3: Roads were re-categorised and renumbered by a January 2016 bylaw; old numbers still appear on older signs and maps (for example the coast road M-1 was once M-2)
column6: M-1 = Adriatic coast road; M-2 = Podgorica to the north.

column2: A motorway, N national, E
column3: A and N numbers form one system. Motorways 1-8 form a broken spider web centred on Amsterdam; A9 is a partial ring and A10 the full ring. N number ranges roughly match provinces (400-430 Utrecht, 430-500 South Holland, 500-550 North Holland, 950-999 Groningen)
column6: A10 = Amsterdam ring.

column2: E, A1-A4 main state roads/motorways (older maps: M-1 to M-6), R regional, local 3-digit
column3: A1 Tabanovce-Kumanovo-Veles-Gevgelija (Serbia-Greece corridor); A2 Deve Bair-Kriva Palanka-Kumanovo-Skopje-Tetovo-Gostivar-Kicevo-Struga-Qafe Thane; A3 Delcevo-Stip-Veles-Prilep-Bitola-Ohrid; A4 Skopje-Stip-Strumica. Local 3-digit roads: first digit sets a zone (1 centre, 2 north-east, 3 Skopje, 4 west, 5 east, 6 south-east)
column4: A1 north-south; A2 and A3 cross the country east-west
column6: A1 = the Serbia-Greece motorway through Veles.

column2: E, Rv national, Fv county
column3: First digit of 2-3 digit national roads is a zone: 1 around Oslo, 2 north and east of Oslo, 3 west, 4 south, 5 south-west, 6 north-west, 7-9 further north
column4: E: even = E-W; E6 is the main N-S exception
column6: Higher first digit = further north.

column2: E, A motorway, S expressway, DK national, DW provincial
column3: Motorways share the number of the national road. One-digit DK roads form the main grid. 3-digit DK: first digit zone from 1 north-west to 9 south-east
column4: 1-2 digit DK: even = E-W, odd = N-S
column6: DK numbers match the A/S number on the same corridor.

column2: E, A motorway, IP, IC, N national (<400), M municipal (>400)
column3: IP1-IP3 run N-S, IP4-IP8 run E-W. Lower N numbers usually mean longer routes
column6: IP1 = Porto-Lisbon-Algarve.

column2: A, E, DN national, DJ county, DC communal
column3: DN and DJ use a zone system by first digit (seven zones bounded by trunk roads radiating clockwise from Bucharest; no numbers start with 8 or 9). In each zone numbers generally rise with the shortest distance to Bucharest
column6: DN1 = Bucharest to Brasov and onward to the north-west.

column2: E, M federal main, A national (3 digits), R regional
column3: M1-M10 are the main roads from Moscow (M1 to Minsk, M10 to St Petersburg), numbered counterclockwise. A numbers start near Moscow at A100 and run to A349; first digit zone 1 Russia, 2 west, 3 Caucasus and Central Asia
column6: M-roads leave Moscow; M1 west, M4 south, M7 east.

column2: Not covered
column3: Not covered
column6: Not covered.

column2: A (class IA), expressways IM, IB (2-digit), IIA (3-digit starting 1 or 2), IIB (3-digit)
column3: Motorways are one-digit A numbers; IB two digits; IIA three digits
column6: A1 runs Belgrade-Nis; signs are blue for expressways.

column2: D motorway (D1-D4), R expressway (R1-R7), national roads (plain), I ring roads
column3: 3-digit national roads start with 4 or 5 (zone); most 2-digit start with 5, 6, 7. A Z suffix = zapad (west). Ring road numbers increase from the city centre
column6: Plain 3-digit number = second-class road.

column2: A motorway (A1-A9), H fast road, G main (G1-G12), R regional, E
column3: Numbers are sequential within each class; each number is unique nationwide; A1 and A2 form a cross
column4: Only motorways described: A1 SW-NE, A2 NW-SE
column6: A1 Koper-Ljubljana-Maribor; A2 to Karawanken.

column2: E, AP/A motorways, A autovia, N national (Roman numerals I-VI and 3-digit), C regional, provincial codes
column3: Six zones bounded by the radial N roads; a road starting in a zone keeps that zone's first digit; AP1-AP6 and A1-A6 radiate clockwise from Madrid. Catalan C numbers follow direction (C1x N-S, C2x W-E, C3x SW-NE, C4x-C6x SE-NW)
column6: A-1 north, A-2 north-east, A-3 east, A-4 south, A-5 west, A-6 north-west of Madrid.

column2: Local Norwegian designations
column3: Not covered
column6: Not covered.

column2: E, riksvag 1-2 digit, primary county roads 3-digit (100-404), secondary county 500+
column3: National roads are numbered from south to north; primary county roads rise from 100 in the south to 404 in the north. Secondary road numbers are not signed. Where a national road follows an E road, both numbers appear
column6: Blue signs; E4 and E6 are the long N-S backbones.

column2: E, A motorway, main roads (plain 1-30 signed), cantonal K
column3: Main road numbers 101-499 increase eastward; lower numbers are more important. Motorway exits are numbered sequentially
column6: A1 runs Geneva-St Gallen across the Plateau.

column2: E, O. motorway, D. national (3 digits), province roads (2 digits + dash + 2 digits)
column3: Motorway zones: 1 north-west, 2 centre, 3 west, 5 south-east. National roads: E-W routes are even and rise southward, N-S routes are odd (500+) and rise eastward. Most important E-W end in 00/0, most important N-S end in 50/5. Provincial roads start with the province code (06 Ankara, 34 Istanbul)
column6: D100 is the long northern E-W road (Edirne-Istanbul-Bolu-Erzurum); O-4 links Istanbul and Ankara.

column2: E, M international (M01-M11), N national, R regional, T territorial
column3: M01-M07 run clockwise around Kyiv; M09-M11 run anticlockwise around Lviv; N numbers sequential; R roughly west to east; T first two digits = oblast code
column6: M06 = Kyiv to Uzhhorod; M05 = Kyiv to Odesa.

column2: A, B, M motorway; Northern Ireland has its own separate numbering
column3: Great Britain: A1-A6 radiate clockwise from London (A1 north to Edinburgh, A2 to Dover); A7-A9 radiate clockwise from Edinburgh. Great Britain is split into nine zones; a road's first digit shows the zone it starts in (zone 1 between A1 and A2). Motorways have their own zones clockwise from M1
column6: Numbers starting with 1 = east of the A1 and north of the Thames; E-roads are not signed in the UK.
